name: Archie DAW (desktop)
about: Everything the desktop program can do, as tools an assistant (Archie, a hosted agent) can call. One entry per bridge command, kept in step with desktop-host/Source/Bridge.h by tests/desktopStudioTools.test.ts: a command with no entry fails the test. Add the entry in the same change as the command.

classes.edit: changes the project or the live setup; reversible, local to this computer
classes.dialog: opens a window or file dialog that the PERSON must answer; an assistant asks the person first
classes.test: only exists when the program is started in test mode; never offered

chainIds: A plug-in chain is addressed by one number: 0.. is a track, 100..107 is FX return 1..8, 200 is the master inserts.
units: Beats are quarter notes. Levels are dB. Pan is -1 (left) to 1 (right).

tools.name: hello
tools.summary: Program name, version, how many tracks, and what it can do.

tools.name: getState
tools.summary: The whole current state: tracks (plug-in chains, sends, levels), FX returns, master section, plug-in list, MIDI devices, audio device, and the transport.

tools.name: play
tools.summary: Start the shared transport.

tools.name: stop
tools.summary: Stop in place; a second stop returns to the start.

tools.name: pause
tools.summary: Stop and keep the position (sends MMC pause).

tools.name: toggle
tools.summary: Play if stopped, stop if playing.

tools.name: record
tools.summary: Switch recording on or off (notes from armed or selected tracks are captured while playing; a count-in runs first if set).

tools.name: locate
tools.summary: Move the playhead.

tools.name: bpm
tools.summary: Set the tempo at the start of the song.

tools.name: timesig
tools.summary: Set the time signature at the start of the song.

tools.name: tap
tools.summary: Tap tempo: call once for each tap; from the third tap on the song's tempo follows what is being tapped (the last 8 taps, odd ones thrown out, a gap over 2 seconds starts again). Returns the tempo and how many taps have been heard.

tools.name: tempoAdd
tools.summary: Add a tempo change at a beat (a step change).

tools.name: tempoRemove
tools.summary: Remove a tempo change by its position in the tempo map (the first entry cannot be removed).

tools.name: loop
tools.summary: Turn the loop on or off and set its start and end.

tools.name: swing
tools.summary: Groove: delay every second grid step of the note clips. amount 0 (straight) to 1 (a full triplet feel); grid 0.5 for eighths or 0.25 for sixteenths. It bends the notes as they play and leaves the clips as they are.

tools.name: countIn
tools.summary: Bars of count-in before recording starts.

tools.name: metronome
tools.summary: Click on or off.

tools.name: ppqn
tools.summary: Tick resolution used for display and quantising.

tools.name: sync
tools.summary: Follow: 0 internal clock, 1 MIDI clock in, 2 MIDI timecode in.

tools.name: fps
tools.summary: Timecode frame rate: 0 = 24, 1 = 25, 2 = 29.97 drop, 3 = 30.

tools.name: tcOffset
tools.summary: Timecode at the start of the song, in seconds.

tools.name: clockOut
tools.summary: Send MIDI clock to the chosen MIDI output (this drives other equipment).

tools.name: mtcOut
tools.summary: Send MIDI timecode to the chosen MIDI output.

tools.name: mmcOut
tools.summary: Send MIDI Machine Control (play, stop, record, locate) to the chosen MIDI output; this can start other equipment.

tools.name: mmcIn
tools.summary: Obey MIDI Machine Control from MIDI inputs.

tools.name: mmcDevice
tools.summary: MMC device id (127 = all).

tools.name: midiIn
tools.summary: Listen to a MIDI input or stop listening (ids are in getState).

tools.name: midiOut
tools.summary: Choose the MIDI output for clock, timecode and MMC (empty string = none).

tools.name: track
tools.summary: (compKey and gateKey: the uid of the track the compressor or gate listens to as a side-chain, 0 = this track's own sound.) Change one setting of a track. Key colour takes a palette number 0-30 (names in tools/studio-palette.json) or -1 for none. Key patPlay is how the track's step pattern (its note clips) plays: 0 off, 1 loop (the default), 2 one shot (once from the start of each clip, then silent). Key patTrans moves the pattern up or down in semitones (-24 to 24, 0 by default). Both can be automated with automationLane kinds 6 (Pattern play) and 5 (Pattern transpose). Key inGainDb is the channel input gain in dB (-24 to 24, applied where the sound enters the channel's effects, after the instrument) and inInvert (true or false) flips the channel's polarity; both are neutral at 0 and false. The channel EQ is a high-pass and a low-pass filter (12 dB per octave): eqHpOn and eqLpOn (true or false), eqHpHz (20 to 2000) and eqLpHz (1000 to 20000); both are off by default. The channel compressor is compOn (true or false, off by default), compThr (threshold -40 to 0 dB, -18 by default), compRatio (1.1 to 20, 4 by default), compRel (release 0.05 to 1.2 seconds, 0.3 by default), compFast (true for a 0.5 ms attack instead of 5 ms), compPeak (true for a peak detector, false for RMS) and compMakeup (0 to 24 dB); it runs before the gate and the EQ. The channel gate is gateOn (true or false, off by default), gateExp (true for a gentle 2:1 expander instead of a gate), gateFast (true for a faster attack), gateThr (threshold -80 to 0 dB, -45 by default), gateRange (how far it turns the sound down, 0 to 80 dB, 40 by default), gateRel (release 0.05 to 4 seconds, 0.3 by default) and gateHold (0 to 2 seconds, 0.05 by default). width is the channel's stereo width from 0 (mono) to 2 (twice as wide), 1 by default (unchanged); it works on a stereo sound's side signal, never changes a mono sound, and sits after the effects and before the pan. groove (1 to 31, or -1 for none) is the groove channel the track's note clips play through.

key.desc: source (0 off, 1 input, 2 tone, 3 noise, 4 impulse, 5 sweep, 6 file), gainDb, pan, inGainDb, inInvert, eqHpOn, eqHpHz, eqLpOn, eqLpHz, compOn, compThr, compRatio, compRel, compFast, compPeak, compMakeup, gateOn, gateExp, gateFast, gateThr, gateRange, gateRel, gateHold, width, groove, mute, solo, armed, name

tools.name: masterDb
tools.summary: Master level.

tools.name: sendOn
tools.summary: Switch one of a track's sends (0 to 7) on or off. Nothing reaches the FX return of that number unless the send is on. The send keeps its level while off.

tools.name: sendLevel
tools.summary: Set the level of one of a track's sends (0 to 7), -60 to +6 dB. It is that track's own amount into the effect and does not change any other track. It does not switch the send on or off.

tools.name: sendPre
tools.summary: Choose whether one of a track's sends (0 to 7) takes its sound before the fader (pre) or after it (post).

tools.name: send
tools.summary: Set a track's send (0 to 7) level and whether it is tapped before the fader (pre) or after it. (The older way: a level above off switches the send on, -100 switches it off.)

tools.name: ret
tools.summary: Change one setting of an FX return (0 to 7).

tools.name: addTrack
tools.summary: Add a track (up to 32).

tools.name: removeTrack
tools.summary: Remove a track and the plug-ins on it (any track; the ones after it move up). Without a track number it removes the last one. Undo puts it back.

tools.name: selectTrack
tools.summary: Select a track: hardware MIDI goes to it when no track is armed.

tools.name: noteOn
tools.summary: Play a note on a track now.

tools.name: noteOff
tools.summary: Release a note.

tools.name: noteTrace
tools.summary: Save the last notes every track sent to its plug-in (the beat each one was placed at, on or off, note, velocity) to Documents/Archie DAW note trace.txt, to find a note that sounds when it should not.

tools.name: panic
tools.summary: Silence everything: release every note on every track (all sound off and all notes off on all 16 channels) and reset every plug-in so hung voices and delay or reverb tails end. It does not stop the transport and changes no setting.

tools.name: allNotesOff
tools.summary: Release every note on a track.

tools.name: setClip
tools.summary: Replace a track's MIDI pattern: a length in beats and notes (beat, len, note, vel, ch).

tools.name: getClip
tools.summary: Read a track's MIDI pattern.

tools.name: clearClip
tools.summary: Remove a track's MIDI pattern.

tools.name: scan
tools.summary: Look for VST3 plug-ins (the Local Builder's output and the standard folder) in separate processes.

tools.name: addPlugin
tools.summary: Put a known plug-in on a chain.

tools.name: removePlugin
tools.summary: Remove a plug-in from a chain (its state is lost).

tools.name: moveSlot
tools.summary: Move a plug-in up or down its chain.

tools.name: bypass
tools.summary: Bypass a plug-in or switch it back on.

tools.name: deviceExtras
tools.summary: Read what an Archie device shares with the website besides its parameters (for Archie Drums: the pattern on view), with what its saved state looks like. For checking the connection.

tools.name: deviceLinkAll
tools.summary: Connect every Archie device in the rack (Archie Drums) to the person's Ask Archie account in one go, or disconnect them all. Each copy of a device has its own connection, so several copies connect separately. Connecting may open their browser to confirm each new one.

tools.name: deviceShow
tools.summary: Show a connected Archie device on the Ask Archie website: tells the site it is the one to display and opens the page in the person's browser.

tools.name: deviceLink
tools.summary: Connect an Archie device (Archie Drums) in the rack to the person's Ask Archie account, or disconnect it. Connecting opens their browser for them to confirm; once connected, Archie and the website can read and change its parameters.

tools.name: getArrangement
tools.summary: Read a track's clips on the timeline: each instance (id, start, length, offset, contentId) and the shared content they point at.

tools.name: addInstance
tools.summary: Put a clip on a track's timeline: either a new clip (clip) or another instance of an existing clip (contentId), which stays shared.

length.desc: beats; 0 or left out = as long as the clip

tools.name: setInstance
tools.summary: Move, resize, crop or change a clip instance: start, length, offset, trimStart (crop the front to a beat); colour (palette number 0-30, -1 = take the track colour); muted (true = the clip is silent but kept); label (the clip's own name, empty = none); for an audio clip also warp (true makes the sound follow the tempo), srcBpm (the tempo it was made at), sourceBeats (or: this whole sound is N beats long), repitch (true = pitch moves with speed instead of keeping pitch), transpose (semitones, -24 to 24, hundredths allowed: the clip's pitch moves and its length and timing stay; 0 = the original sound; made in the background, the clip reads pitchState off, rendering or ready), keepFormant (true, the default, keeps a voice's colour when the pitch moves), gainDb (-60 to 24), fadeIn and fadeOut (seconds, at least 0.0005) and reverse (true plays it backwards). A longer instance loops the clip.

tools.name: removeInstance
tools.summary: Delete one clip instance (the clip's other instances stay).

tools.name: duplicateInstance
tools.summary: Copy a clip instance to another place or track; shared (default) means editing one changes both.

tools.name: makeUnique
tools.summary: Give a clip instance content of its own so editing it no longer changes its copies.

tools.name: splitInstance
tools.summary: Cut a clip instance in two at a beat; both halves keep the same content.

tools.name: quantiseNotes
tools.summary: Move the starts of a note clip's notes toward the nearest grid line (strength 1 = exactly on it, 0.5 = half way); with lengths, the ends too. All notes, or only the listed indices. Every copy of the clip changes.

tools.name: transposeNotes
tools.summary: Move a note clip's notes up or down by semitones (kept within 0 to 127). All notes, or only the listed indices.

tools.name: editContent
tools.summary: (A note clip may also carry ctls: a list of [beat, type, value, channel], type 128 = pitch bend 0..16383 with 8192 centre, else controller 1, 64 or 11 with 0..127. Leave ctls out to keep what the clip has.) Replace the notes of a clip's content: every instance of it, on any track, changes together.

tools.name: masterSound
tools.summary: Change the Archie sound at the end of the master: amOn (true or false), amCut (true or false: the 20 Hz cutoff, a 24 dB per octave high-pass that keeps sub-bass from taking limiter headroom), amPush (0 to 18 dB of extra level into the limiter, the loud-max control), amDrive (0 to 1: warmth and a little harmonic that rounds the peaks), amCeil (-3 to 0 dB: the loudest the output can be, held by a look-ahead limiter), amBass (0 to 6 dB low shelf at 90 Hz), amTone (-3 to +3 dB high shelf at 6 kHz) and amTarget (a loudness target in LUFS, -23 to -6, or 0 for none: push then follows the short-term loudness of the finished mix by itself, upward only). Key amResetLufs starts the integrated loudness again. The master fader is the input to it. Off, the master is unchanged. A new song starts with it on, drive 0.25 and ceiling -1 dB.

tools.name: cue
tools.summary: Hot cues: three stored loops, index 0 to 2 (cue 1 is always there). op trigger jumps to that cue (on the loopJump point while playing) and it repeats until another is triggered; here makes a loop at the current bar on an empty cue; set gives it start and end in beats; remove clears cue 2 or 3; learn waits for the next controller pad and assigns it; unlearn forgets it.

tools.name: loopJump
tools.summary: Hot cue: when a moved loop takes effect while the song plays. mode 0 at once, 1 at the next 16th note, 2 at the next beat, 3 at the end of the bar, 4 at the end of the loop that is playing. The song then jumps to the start of the new loop.

tools.name: eq
tools.summary: Change one setting of a channel EQ (a track by number, or 200 for the master). Four parametric bands: b0 is a low shelf, b1 and b2 are bells, b3 is a high shelf. Keys b0on b1on b2on b3on (1 or 0), b0hz to b3hz (20 to 20000), b0gain to b3gain (-18 to 18 dB), b0q to b3q (0.3 wide to 10 narrow), and the filters hpOn, hpHz (20 to 2000), lpOn, lpHz (1000 to 20000). A band that is off, or at 0 dB, changes nothing.

chain.desc: a track number, or 200 for the master

tools.name: getEq
tools.summary: Read a channel EQ: the four bands (on, hz, gain, q) and the high-pass and low-pass filters.

chain.desc: a track number, or 200 for the master

tools.name: eqSpectrum
tools.summary: The spectrum of the sound after a channel EQ: 96 points from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, in dB below full scale (-100 is nothing). Only fills while the song plays.

chain.desc: a track number, or 200 for the master

tools.name: openEqWindow
tools.summary: Open the EQ of a track or the master in its own window.

chain.desc: a track number, or 200 for the master

tools.name: openPanelWindow
tools.summary: Open the Track Panel (a track, FX return or the master) in its own window that stays on top.

tools.name: popOutView
tools.summary: Open the Strips, the Rack, the Mixer or the Settings in its own window (for a second screen). The window keeps its place and size, follows the same song live, and can be closed with its own close button.

page.desc: for settings: ui, browsing, audio, midi, sync, controls, folders or account

tools.name: audioOption
tools.summary: Change an audio option saved with the program: playInBackground (false lets the sound card go while another program is in front), renderWithCardBuffer (true makes exports and bounces work in pieces the size of the sound card buffer), masterTuneCents (-100 to 100: retunes AUDIO CLIPS only, never instruments or plug-ins), latencyAdjustMs (milliseconds, -200 to 200, added to the sound card's reported latency when a recording is placed: raise it if recorded audio plays back too late) and maxThreads (0 to 7 audio threads, or -1 for a sensible number for this computer; it takes effect the next time the program starts).

tools.name: groove
tools.summary: (Also: key pre = pre-align notes to the grid before the groove, glob = use the Global shuffle; key globalShuffle (0 to 100) sets that one shared value, with any ch.) Change one setting of a groove channel (ch 1 to 31: A2 to D8 in the Groove dock; channel A1 is the global swing, command swing). A channel plays a groove patch through its strength, and notes played through it come out a little earlier or later, louder or softer, longer or shorter, without changing the clip. Keys: on (true or false), patch (the name of a built-in or extracted groove, or empty for none), strength (0 to 1; 0 does nothing at all), timing, vel and len (the impacts, percent of the patch's own amounts, 0 to 200, 100 by default), rand (random timing in ticks of 480 to the beat, 0 to 120, repeatable), slide (all notes later or earlier, percent of a step, -50 to 50), shuffle (a swing on every second step, 0 to 100) and anchor (which step of the pattern lines up with the clip start, 0 to 63). To play a track or a clip through a channel use the track command with key groove, or setInstance with groove.

tools.name: extractGroove
tools.summary: Make a groove patch from the playing of a note clip: for each step of a one-bar cycle, how early or late its notes are, how loud and how long, relative to the clip's averages. grid 0.25 (sixteenths, the default) or 0.5 (eighths). Returns how many patches there are now and the new patch's name; choose it on a channel with the groove command's patch key.

tools.name: deleteGroove
tools.summary: Delete a groove patch you extracted (the built-in ones cannot be deleted). A channel that used it plays straight again.

tools.name: controlRoom
tools.summary: Change one setting of the control room, the monitoring feed that goes to the sound card (a bounce or an export is never changed by it). crDb is its level in dB (-90 to 6, 0 by default), crDim (true or false) turns it down a further 20 dB, and crPair chooses where it comes out: 0 is the main outputs (1 and 2), 1 is outputs 3 and 4, 2 is 5 and 6 and so on up to 8, in which case the main outputs carry the master unchanged. A pair the sound card does not have falls back to the main outputs.

tools.name: masterComp
tools.summary: (Also mcKey: the uid of the track whose sound the compressor listens to, 0 = the mix itself.) Change one setting of the master compressor, which compresses the whole mix after the master inserts and before the master fader. mcOn (true or false, off by default), mcPeak (true for a peak detector, false for RMS, the default), mcThr (threshold -40 to 0 dB, -12 by default), mcRatio (1.1 to 20, 2 by default), mcAtk (attack 0.0001 to 0.03 seconds, 0.01 by default), mcRel (release 0.05 to 1.2 seconds, 0.3 by default) and mcMakeup (0 to 24 dB). Off, it changes nothing.

key.desc: mcOn, mcPeak, mcThr, mcRatio, mcAtk, mcRel or mcMakeup

tools.name: closeWindow
tools.summary: Close one of the windows of their own: key is strips, rack, mixer, settings, eq or panel.

tools.name: quit
tools.summary: Close the program. Anything in the open song that is not saved is lost.

tools.name: closePanelWindow
tools.summary: Close the floating Track Panel window.

tools.name: setDeviceMeta
tools.summary: Mark a plug-in as a favourite and/or give it tags in the device browser (kept with the plug-in list, not in a project). getState lists every device with kind (instrument, effect or utility), categories, favourite, tags and how often it has been used.

tags.desc: the complete list of tags (replaces the old list)

tools.name: moveSlotTo
tools.summary: Move a device to a place in the same rack or into another rack (a track, FX return or the master): the same plug-in, with its settings and window. Returns the place it ended up.

track.desc: the chain the device is in

toTrack.desc: the chain to move it to; left out = the same one

to.desc: the place in that chain (0 = first)

tools.name: importAudio
tools.summary: Put a sound file (wav, aiff, flac, mp3, ogg) on a track as an audio clip at a beat (default: the playhead). The clip is as long as the sound; make it longer to repeat it, trim its front with setInstance trimStart, split it with splitInstance. The sound plays at its own speed.

path.desc: the full path of a file on this computer

tools.name: chopInstance
tools.summary: Cut a clip into pieces that share its sound: at the places the sound's hits are (mode hits, with sensitivity 0 to 1) or every grid beats (mode grid). The pieces together play exactly what the clip did. Returns how many pieces.

tools.name: quantiseClips
tools.summary: Move clip starts toward the nearest grid line (strength 1 = exactly on it, 0.5 = half way); with fill, a clip that now runs into the next one is shortened to end where the next begins. Default: every audio clip on the track. Returns how many changed.

instances.desc: clip instance ids; left out = all audio clips on the track

tools.name: getAutomation
tools.summary: The automation lanes of a channel (track 0.. or FX return 100..): each lane's id, what it controls (kind 0 level in dB, 1 pan -1..1, 2 a plug-in parameter 0..1), its on/off and its points { beat, value }.

tools.name: getParams
tools.summary: The parameters of the plug-in in a rack slot, so one can be automated: { index, name, value } (value 0..1).

tools.name: automationLane
tools.summary: Add, remove or switch a channel's automation lane. op add: kind 0 level, 1 pan, 2 plug-in parameter (with slot and param), 3 input gain (tracks only, -24 to 24 dB), 4 a send level (with slot), 5 step pattern transpose (tracks only, -24 to 24 semitones, whole steps), 6 step pattern play (tracks only, 0 off, 1 loop, 2 one shot), 7 mute and 8 solo (tracks only, 0 or 1); on the master (chain 200) the Archie sound: 9 push (0 to 18 dB), 10 drive (0 to 1), 11 ceiling (-3 to 0 dB), 12 bass (0 to 6 dB), 13 tone (-3 to 3 dB), 14 Archie sound on (0 or 1), 15 the 20 Hz cut (0 or 1); and 16 an EQ setting of a track or the master, with param 0 to 19: 0 to 15 is band param/4 with param%4 = on, frequency, gain, Q (b1 is band 2), 16 high-pass on, 17 high-pass frequency, 18 low-pass on, 19 low-pass frequency. A gain lane holds dB (-18 to 18); frequency and Q lanes hold 0 to 1 on a logarithmic scale (band frequency = 20 x 1000^v Hz, Q = 0.3 x (10/0.3)^v, high-pass = 20 x 100^v Hz, low-pass = 1000 x 20^v Hz); on lanes hold 0 or 1; asking again for the same target returns the lane it already has.

tools.name: autoRecord
tools.summary: Switch Record automation on or off. On, and with the song playing, moving a Level, Pan or Input gain control, or a control in a plug-in's own window (the plug-in must report it to the host, as most do), writes that control's lane at the song's position, making the lane if there is none. The lane does not pull the control back while it is held. One take is one undo step. The state's autoLearn.record says whether it is on.

tools.name: autoLearn
tools.summary: Learn a plug-in parameter for automation: start it on a channel (on true), then move a control in one of that channel's plug-ins' own windows. The first parameter that moves (one the host may automate; parameters that move by themselves are ignored) gets its automation lane made, and the state's autoLearn says which (found, lane, slot, param, label). It gives up after 20 seconds (timedOut). on false stops it. The master has no lanes.

tools.name: setAutomationPoints
tools.summary: Replace all the points of an automation lane: [{ beat, value }] (sorted for you; level in dB -90..12, pan -1..1, plug-in parameters 0..1). While the song plays the channel follows the lane; between points it moves in a straight line, before the first and after the last it holds.

tools.name: exportAudio
tools.summary: Mix the song (or part of it) down to a wav file: opens a save box, then renders faster than real time on a private copy of the program's engine, so playing can go on. bits 16, 24 (default) or 32 (floating point); from and to in beats (left out = the whole song); tail = seconds of ring-out after the end (default 2). Progress and the result (file, seconds, peakDb, clipped) come as export events.

tools.name: exportMidi
tools.summary: Write the song's note clips as a standard MIDI file (type 1, 480 ticks a quarter note, tempo map and time signatures, one track per track that has notes). Opens a save box. Audio clips are not included.

tools.name: importMidi
tools.summary: Read a standard MIDI file: each track with notes becomes a new track holding a note clip from the start, and the file's tempo and time signature become the song's. Controllers and pitch bend are not kept. One undo step.

tools.name: bounce
tools.summary: Play one clip through its own track (instrument, effects, sends and master) and write the sound. mode: place (to a new track, original clip muted), recording (to a new track as a new recording, original kept), sample (a wav in the bounced-samples folder only), disk (opens a save box). The clip needs a length. tail = seconds of ring-out (default 2). Progress comes as export events and the result as a bounce event.

tools.name: copyChannel
tools.summary: Copy a whole channel (sound source, level, pan, colour, clips, automation, plug-ins with their settings, sends) to the channel clipboard.

tools.name: cutChannel
tools.summary: Copy the LAST track to the channel clipboard and remove it (tracks cannot yet be taken out of the middle).

tools.name: pasteChannel
tools.summary: Add a new track at the end from the channel clipboard (clips are new copies, plug-ins load again with their settings). One undo step.

tools.name: duplicateChannel
tools.summary: Add a copy of a track at the end, called 'name copy', with its clips (as new copies), plug-ins and settings. One undo step.

tools.name: newProject
tools.summary: Start a new empty song (the starting tracks with nothing on them, 120 bpm). Whatever was open and not saved is lost, so the person confirms first.

tools.name: getFiles
tools.summary: The recent songs (newest first), the saved templates, and the file Save writes to (empty = a new song).

tools.name: openRecent
tools.summary: Open a song from the recent list by its full path. Whatever was open and not saved is lost.

tools.name: clearRecent
tools.summary: Forget the recent songs list (the song files themselves are not touched).

tools.name: saveTemplate
tools.summary: Keep the current song as a template under a name; New from Template starts a new song from it.

tools.name: newFromTemplate
tools.summary: Start a new song from a saved template. Whatever was open and not saved is lost.

tools.name: recoverSession
tools.summary: After the program was closed by a crash: open the song that was kept (it is kept every minute) as a new, unsaved song. The older kept copy stays as recovery-previous.archiestudio.

tools.name: dismissRecovery
tools.summary: Decline the offer to recover the song kept before a crash (a copy stays as recovery-previous.archiestudio).

tools.name: testCrash
tools.summary: Test copy only: make a thread of the program fault on purpose, to prove the crash note (crash-module.bin) is written.

tools.name: openManual
tools.summary: Open the Archie DAW manual (an HTML page installed with the program) in the default browser.

tools.name: getCrashed
tools.summary: Plug-ins that stopped the program while they were loading (id, name, how many times). Loading one of these is refused unless addPlugin is sent with force true.

tools.name: forgetCrash
tools.summary: Remove a plug-in from the crashed list so it loads without the warning again.

tools.name: joinInstance
tools.summary: Join a clip with the next clip on its track: pieces of one sound that carry on from each other become one clip; two note clips become one holding both sets of notes. Refused for two different sounds. One undo step.

tools.name: audioToMidi
tools.summary: Turn the hits of an audio clip into notes: a new track with a note clip, one short middle-C note at each hit. It finds when, not what pitch. sensitivity 0..1 (default 0.5). One undo step.

tools.name: unusedRecordings
tools.summary: List the recordings in the recordings folder that no clip in this song uses (count, megabytes, file names). Another saved song may still use one.

tools.name: deleteUnusedRecordings
tools.summary: Move the unused recordings to the Recycle Bin. Needs confirm true, sent only after the person has seen the list from unusedRecordings.

tools.name: cancelExport
tools.summary: Stop an audio export that is running (the half-written file is deleted).

tools.name: warpMarker
tools.summary: Warp markers: pin a moment of a warped sound clip to a beat on the timeline, so a part that drifts (a drummer, a voice) is pulled onto the grid; between markers the sound is stretched evenly, and the clip's front stays put. op set (pin the moment sec of the sound to timeline beat; moves the marker already there), remove (by index) or clear. Refused if it would run the sound backwards or stretch a part more than 4x.

tools.name: detectTempo
tools.summary: A guess at the tempo (beats a minute) a sound was made at, from where its hits fall, with a confidence from 0 to 1. Changes nothing; use setInstance srcBpm to apply it.

tools.name: getTransients
tools.summary: Where the sound of an audio clip starts a new hit or note, as seconds from the start of the sound (it listens for sudden loudness, not for pitch or tempo). Higher sensitivity finds smaller starts. With instance instead of contentId it returns each hit as heard on that clip's timeline: { sec, beat } with warp and markers applied.

tools.name: getWaveform
tools.summary: The waveform of an audio clip's sound as numbers from 0 to 1 (the loudest point in each stretch), for drawing.

tools.name: getUserKeymap
tools.summary: The person's own keyboard shortcuts (the ones they changed from the defaults): { command: [keys] }.

tools.name: setUserKeymap
tools.summary: Change the keys for a command (a tool name or a ui.* action from the keymap); with no keys, put the default back.

keys.desc: e.g. ["Ctrl+Shift+X"]; left out = back to the default

tools.name: resetKeymap
tools.summary: Put every keyboard shortcut back to its default.

tools.name: undo
tools.summary: Undo the last edit (mixer settings, patterns, tempo, tracks, plug-ins on a chain). A fader drag is one step. Returns the label of what was undone.

tools.name: redo
tools.summary: Do again the edit that was just undone.

tools.name: openEditor
tools.summary: Open a plug-in's own window on the person's screen.

tools.name: analyse
tools.summary: Measure a plug-in in a separate process: response, level and distortion, aliasing, noise, stability (effects); pitch, harmonics, off-harmonic energy, onset, release (instruments). Takes seconds to a minute.

id.desc: a plug-in id instead of track and slot

tools.name: cancelAnalysis
tools.summary: Stop a running analysis.

tools.name: getAnalysis
tools.summary: The last analysis result (every number measured, with its conditions, the limits it was held against, and what was not measured).

tools.name: getSkin
tools.summary: The current look.

tools.name: setSkin
tools.summary: Change the look: a name and a set of CSS variables (colours and sizes only).

tools.name: showTab
tools.summary: Switch the program's window between the console and the online pages.

tools.name: openStudioPage
tools.summary: Open an askarchie.net page inside the program.

tools.name: audioSettings
tools.summary: Open the audio device settings window.

tools.name: saveProject
tools.summary: Save the project to a file the person chooses.

tools.name: loadProject
tools.summary: Open a project file the person chooses. Never offered to an assistant: a project names plug-in files to load.

tools.name: loadFile
tools.summary: Open the file chooser and put the chosen sound file on this track as an audio clip at the playhead.

tools.name: loadSkinFile
tools.summary: Open a skin file the person chooses.

tools.name: saveSkinFile
tools.summary: Save the current look to a file the person chooses.

tools.name: testGetProject
tools.summary: Test mode only: the project as data.

tools.name: testSetProject
tools.summary: Test mode only: load a project from data.

tools.name: testMidiIn
tools.summary: Test mode only: inject a MIDI message as if a keyboard sent it.
